claims.text: Varonis's Aug 18 publication describes a three-flaw chain in Copilot Personal: crafted-URL automatic prompt execution, connected-app data collection/exfiltration, and persistent memory poisoning.
The publication states Microsoft shipped server-side patches Aug 18, 2026, names only Copilot Personal (consumer, copilot.microsoft.com), and reports no observed in-the-wild exploitation.
claims.context: Scope/patch statements; vendor confirmation via CVE ID assignment.

claims.text: The CVE identifier CVE-2026-24301 (CVSS 8.8-class, CWE-77) is the tracking ID used across the researcher publication and MSRC.
claims.context: Identifier corroboration; MSRC page bytes uncaptured (JS shell).

limitations.text: MSRC advisory bytes were not captured (retrieved page is a JS shell); vendor severity/product-scope wording is researcher-attributed, not vendor-quoted.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Exploitability details beyond the researcher's account are not independently tested in captured bytes.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.target: One-click chain involved automatic prompt execution, connected-app data exfiltration and persistent-memory poisoning; Varonis says patches shipped Aug 18 and no exploitation was observed. Distinguish Copilot Personal from Microsoft 365 Copilot.
targets.finding: One-click chain (auto-execution, exfiltration, memory poisoning), Aug 18 patches, no observed exploitation, and Personal-vs-M365 scope all supported by the captured researcher publication with CVE-ID vendor corroboration.
